rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Berk-i basar” is a lightning metaphor for the sudden, piercing awareness and terror caused by an overwhelming fatal event, as the familiar world seems to vanish.
rows.anchor: gözün şimşek çakması, nâgehan tepesinde çakan şimşekten mâruz olduğu dehşet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may describe an ordinary lunar eclipse caused by Earth’s shadow between the Sun and Moon.
rows.anchor: Kamer’in Şems’e istikbâli hâlinde aralarına Arz gölgesinin haylûleti demek olan mâruf Ay tutulmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ordinary eclipse is too slight; the verse more likely describes the Moon’s light vanishing or becoming dim and veiled on that Day.
rows.anchor: hafif kalır. Bu daha ziyade o güne mahsus bir tecellî olmak üzere nûr-i Kamer’in zâil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sun and Moon are shaken from their places and brought together; unlike a conjunction, both disappear into nonexistence.
rows.anchor: Ve Şems ü Kamer cem‘olunur, toplanır şimşek manzarasında olduğu gibi kurs-ı Şems ile kurs-ı Kamer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mefer” is a mim-form verbal noun meaning flight; the impious person frantically seeks somewhere to flee in terror.
rows.anchor: “Mefer”, firar mânasına mimli masdardır. O fâcir insan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Where is escape?” is a rhetorical question expressing despair, though it may also be a genuine question asked in bewilderment.
rows.anchor: şaşkınlıkla hakīkī istifham da olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Wazar” originally means a heavy, steep, fortified mountain, hence a place of refuge.
rows.anchor: sarp ve muhkem dağ demektir. Böyle dağlar firârîlerin sığındıkları yerler olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because fugitives shelter there, “wazar” extends to any refuge or protector, including a mountain, fortress, weapon, person, or shield.
rows.anchor: gerek dağ, gerek kale, gerek silah, gerek insan ve sâire mutlaka melce’, sığınak, sığınacak yer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem illustrates that a young man has no refuge from death or old age.
rows.anchor: لَعَمْرُكَ مَا لِلْفَتَى مِنْ وَزَر مِنَ الْمَوْتِ يُدْرِكُهُ وَالْكِبَرُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day, settlement and final recourse are to the Lord alone.
rows.anchor: Rabbinedir o gün ancak karar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mustaqarr” can be a verbal noun for settling or a place noun for the final abode.
rows.anchor: “Müstekar” istikrar mânasına mimli masdardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every servant’s only refuge is God; those fleeing Him find no other shelter, and all finally reach Him or His command.
rows.anchor: O’ndan kaçmak isteyenler de o gün O’ndan başka sığınacak hiçbir penâh bulamazlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God determines whether each person’s final destination is Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: insanların varacakları karargâhı cennet mi cehennem mi tâyin etmek Rabbine aittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is first to the Prophet, the foremost addressee, and thereby to all people, rather than to the fugitive in the scene.
rows.anchor: seyyid-i muhâtabîn olan Resûl-i Ekrem’e, dolayısıyla da ale’l-umûm insanlara beyân-ı hakikattir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is told what he is and what his good or evil consists in; his deeds and true condition are disclosed.
rows.anchor: İnsan o gün ayıtılır; haber verilir yani kendine haber verilir, yahut insanın ne olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What he sent ahead and left behind” can mean earlier and later deeds, or all good and bad acts sent ahead for the afterlife or left undone; all are accounted for.
rows.anchor: Mukaddem ve muahhar yaptıklarıyla evvel yaptığı ve sonra yaptığı amelleriyle yahut yaptığı, âhiret için takdim ettiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human is inwardly perceptive of himself, a conscious rational soul who knows his own actions and witnesses them in conscience.
rows.anchor: insan kendine karşı bir basîrettir. Bu âyet çok şâyân-ı dikkattir. Burada insanın tam hakikati târif edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even while offering excuses, a person knows within his spirit and conscience what he did and whether those excuses are true.
rows.anchor: ne yaptığını, mazeretlerinin doğru olup olmadığını kendi nefsinde, kendi rûh ve vicdânında bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Public approval or excuses cannot alter the truth before God; people should examine themselves sincerely and distinguish right from wrong before acting.
rows.anchor: insan huzûr-ı Hak’ta haddizâtındaki hakikatiyle karşılaşacak, kendisi kendi aleyhine şâhid olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the address were to humanity generally, the pronouns could refer to a person’s inward knowledge: do not rush to voice it, since God gathers and recites it and one should follow.
rows.anchor: hesab başında Hakk’ın huzûrunda vicdânındakini acele söyleyip de işin içinden çıkacağım diye telaş etme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun’s antecedent is not explicit; a universal-human addressee could make it refer to what is within a person, namely conscience.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetteki بِهِۦ zamirlerinin merci‘i zâhir değildir. Hitab mutlak insana olsaydı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the address is specifically to the Prophet and the passage later names the Qur’an, the pronouns first refer to the Qur’an being revealed; an implied antecedent is sufficient, as at 97:1.
rows.anchor: hitab bilhassa Peygamber’e olmak ve sonra da “Kur’an” denilmiş bulunmak itibariyle bu بِهِۦ zamirinin evvelâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exegetes identify the pronouns as referring to the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Onun için tefsirler bu بِهِۦ zamirlerinin Kur’ân’a râci‘olduğunu beyan etmektedirler.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet moved his lips while Qur’an was descending so he could memorize it, and this verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî de bunun sebeb-i nüzûlünü Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr, İbn Abbas’tan şöyle rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should listen while revelation arrives rather than hurry to recite; God undertakes gathering and reciting it, then he follows Gabriel’s completed reading.
rows.anchor: sade dinle, acele okumak için dilini oynatma

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also undertakes the needed clarification, using five forms of explanation: confirmation, interpretation, alteration, replacement, and necessity; Qur’anic verses explain one another.
rows.anchor: Beyân-ı takrir, Beyân-ı tefsir, Beyân-ı tağyir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “Qur’an” is a verbal noun meaning recitation, though it may also mean the recited text.
rows.anchor: “kur’an” isim değil, kıraat mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also teaches people to pause in important matters, listen sincerely to conscience without mixing in selfish impulses, and act accordingly.
rows.anchor: nefsinin temayülâtını karıştırmayarak samimiyet ve teennî ile dinleyip ona göre hareket etmelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying urges consulting one’s heart even when jurists give verdicts; the author also invokes reports on the prayer for guidance.
rows.anchor: اِسْتـَفْتِ قـَلْبَكَ وَلَوْ أَفـْتَاكَ الْمُفْتُون “kalbine danış, müftüler sana fetvâ verseler bile”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred hadith about God becoming a servant’s hearing and sight also supports this inward attentiveness.
rows.anchor: لاَ يـَزَالُ الْعَبْدُ يـَتـَقَرَّبُ إِلَيَّ بِالنـَّوَافِلِ حَتَّى أَكُونَ سَمْعَهُ وَبَصَرَهُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inspiration is not a source of knowledge for ordinary people as prophetic revelation is, but intention governs deeds and conscience is important for sincere action.
rows.anchor: Enbiyânın vahyinden mâ‘adâ ilhâmât umum için esbâb-ı ilimden değil ise de amellerin hükmü niyete bağlı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation discussion is integrated with the preceding account of conscience rather than left as a digression, joining the beginning and end of the passage.
rows.anchor: bu âyetleri bu sûrede bir istitrad hâlinde bırakmayarak evvelini âhirine tamamen yapıştırmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the address to the Prophet comes a general address; “kallā” rejects haste (or means “indeed”), “the immediate” is the world, and people leave the afterlife.
rows.anchor: “Hakkā” mânasına olduğu da söylenmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radiant faces shine with the joy of success and fulfillment.
rows.anchor: Muvaffakiyet neş’esiyle sürur içinde ışılar parıldar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Sunna understand looking toward their Lord as seeing God’s beauty in the afterlife and affirm the vision of God.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i sünnet bu bakışı rü’yet mânasıyla anlayarak âhirette mü’minlerin cemâlullâhı rü’yetini isbat etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Mu‘tezile
rows.claim: The Mu‘tazila, appealing to 7:143, interpret the gaze as waiting.
rows.anchor: Mu‘tezile de bu bakışı intizar mânasına hamleylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bare anticipation is unsuitable because an unfulfilled wait ends in disappointment and pain, not the joy described for the radiant faces.
rows.anchor: gayeye ermeyen intizârın neticesi neş’e değil, inkisâr-ı hayâl ile elem olacağından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other faces grow grim, contract with grief, and darken.
rows.anchor: Nice yüzler de o gün pusarır eleminden ekşir, kararır, pusarır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “ẓann” means knowing with certainty that a crushing calamity will be inflicted on them.
rows.anchor: burada “zann” cezmen ve yakīnen anlamak mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fāqira” denotes a tremendous calamity, from striking the spinal column and breaking the back; another derivation connects it to branding a camel’s nose and stresses the pain of punishment.
rows.anchor: dâhiye-i azîme demektir ki amûd-i fikārîye isabet eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the calamity as “back-breaker” (“belkıran”), matching the Turkish idiom for an event that breaks someone’s back.
rows.anchor: Lisânımızda “filân iş fülânın belini kırdı” tâbiri kullanılmak itibariyle biz buna mealde “belkıran” demeyi muvâfık bulduk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene turns from the cosmic end and afterlife outcomes to death, the individual’s final crisis and first gate into the next life; worldly attachment begins to break its victims already in this world.
rows.anchor: hayât-ı dünyanın sonu ve âhiretin ilk kapısı ve ferdin kıyameti demek olan ölüm ve sekerât-ı mevt hâli tasvir olunarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Kallā idhā” warns those who love the immediate world and begins the depiction of death.
rows.anchor: âcileye mahabbetle âhireti terkten tahzir ve mevt hâlini tasvirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “when it reaches the collarbones” may refer to the soul that loves the world or, by contextual association, to the spirit.
rows.anchor: Zamiri, dünyaya mahabbet eden nefse yahut o karîne ile rûha râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tarāqī” is the plural of “tarquwa,” the collarbones at the base of the neck toward the arms.
rows.anchor: “Turkuve”nin cem‘idir ki boyunun dibinden kollara doğru olan köprücük kemiklerine denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rāq” is a person performing incantatory healing or ruqya, summoned as a last resort; it may broadly be a physical or spiritual healer, especially a spiritual reciter, sought by believers and unbelievers alike.
rows.anchor: rukye, irvâsâ yapan, nâçarlık hâllerinde son bir tedbir olmak üzere müracaat edilen okuyucu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause around “man rāq” prevents unmarked assimilation of nūn into rā’ that would sound like “merrāk,” meaning a soup seller.
rows.anchor: sekte ile bu iltibâs kat‘edilmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause also evokes the moment when breath stops during the death struggle.
rows.anchor: bu lahza nefesin kesildiği bir sekte lahzası olduğuna bir tenbih olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the deathbed the dying person recognizes the event as final separation from the beloved world, its pleasures, and even the limbs.
rows.anchor: ve sezer, anlar o can çekiştiren, nefesi tıkanan muhtazar o demde anlar ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As death’s agony comes, the limbs become confused and the legs twist together.
rows.anchor: Ölüm acısıyla el ayak karışmış, bacak bacağa dolaşmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Masāq” is a mim-form verbal noun for being driven; the person is seized and compelled to God’s presence for reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: “Mesāk” da sevk mânasına mimli masdardır. Yani o gün o kişi yakalanır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For lovers of this world, death is painful and endless separation and exile; for those devoted to the afterlife, the same moment brings release and joyful union.
rows.anchor: bu lahza dünya mahabbetine sargın rûhlar için böyle elîm bir firak, nihâyetsiz bir hicran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Hal” can function as negation (“not”), but here interpreters take it as “qad,” affirming that the event truly or nearly came.
rows.anchor: قد mânasında olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affirmative sense works either as verification/proximity (“truly came” or “nearly came”) or as a rhetorical question whose answer is “yes, it came.”
rows.anchor: Bunun iki vechi vardır. Birisi, “hel” aslında قد mânasına tahkik veya takrib için olmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening emphasizes that humankind appeared late in the history of creation, then explains gradual development, testing, and the divergent fates of unbelievers and the righteous.
rows.anchor: Bununla insan hilkatinin tekvin tarihinde teahhuru tahkik ve takrir olunmuştur ki sonra da bunun hikmeti derece derece terbiye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some take “human” as Adam or Adam’s descendants, the evident sense is the human genus, including every individual.
rows.anchor: hepsine şâmil olan cins-i insandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Raghib, “dahr” in its primary sense is the total duration from the universe’s beginning to its end, and can also mean long, indefinite spans.
rows.anchor: asl-ı mânasında âlemin vücûdunun mebde’inden inkızâsına kadar bütün müddeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike “dahr,” “zamān” can refer to durations both short and long, including the whole sequence of time or its parts; “dahr” denotes the whole or great spans, not an hour, day, or month.
rows.anchor: bunun hilâfına olarak az müddete de çok müddete de denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Companions and jurists disagreed over the minimum duration meant by definite or indefinite “dahr” in oath law; Abu Hanifa suspended judgment on the indefinite form and said he did not know.
rows.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam nekre olan “dehr”in ekall-i[^3] mânasını tâyinde tevakkuf etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ḥīn” is a bounded period, short or long, unlike “dahr,” which can denote the whole.
rows.anchor: “Hîn” zamandan az veya çok mahdud bir müddete denilir. Külle ıtlak edilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The period runs from the universe’s creation to humanity’s creation; it is bounded but its length is unknown relative to humans, and mankind came long after the universe.
rows.anchor: insan cinsi âlemin hilkatinden hayli müddet sonra yaratılmıştır. Âlemin hilkatiyle başlayan dehirden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “There was nothing mentioned” is grammatically a circumstantial clause of “human” or an adjective of “period”; the negation targets being mentioned, not existence itself.
rows.anchor: Ve nefy kayda müteveccihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before humankind appeared as a recognized name and concept, there were precursor things, but nothing yet known or conceived as the human genus.
rows.anchor: Hiçbir şey olmamış değil, mezkur bir şey olmamıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Madhkūr” may derive from dhikr or dhukr; because the point is the concept and referent rather than merely saying “human,” the latter derivation is more apt, though the former is broader.
rows.anchor: Asl-ı mâna mücerred “insan” lafzının söylenmesi değil, bununla kasdolunan mefhum ve medlül olduğu için mazmumdan olmak daha mâkuldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity’s precursors pass through elements and minerals, then plant and animal nourishment, and finally semen, linking the account to 23:12.
rows.anchor: Bidâyetinde ilk maddeleri olan anâsır, me‘âdin, sonra onlardan tavır tavır yaratılıp mütevassıt maddeleri olan nebâtî hayvânî gıdalar سُلَٰلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human genus is originated and contingent, not eternal; it came into being much later than the universe.
rows.anchor: Hakikat insanın her ferdi gibi cinsi de kadîm değildir, hâdistir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raghib defines “nuṭfa” as pure water; the word also denotes male fluid and is commonly treated as synonymous with semen.
rows.anchor: Erkeğin suyuna da “nutfe” denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls the nuṭfa a part of semen, and a Muslim report likewise says a child does not come from all of the fluid but from a portion of it.
rows.anchor: diye nutfenin meniden bir cüz olduğu ifade olunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general statement that humanity comes from a nuṭfa appears to include Adam, while requiring that his nuṭfa did not come from another human; his beginning is from clay.
rows.anchor: Sonra insan cinsinin bir nutfeden yaratılmış olmasının zâhiri Âdem’in de bir nutfeden yaratılmış olduğunu ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although 3:59 might suggest excluding Adam, the dust and clay verses describe humanity’s origin and do not contradict Adam’s beginning from a nonhuman nuṭfa; the general wording excludes no person.
rows.anchor: gibi umûma hitab eden âyetler de mebde’ nokta-i nazarından bunların bütün insanlar hakkında sâdık olduğunu anlattığından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Amshāj” comes from a root meaning to mix, but exegetes dispute whether it is singular or plural.
rows.anchor: “Emşâc”: “Nutfe”ye sıfat yapılan bu kelime, bir şeyi bir şeye karıştırmak

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari in al-Kashshaf prefers a singular adjective for the singular nuṭfa, meaning mixed, and rejects treating the form as a plural.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf müfred olan “nutfe”ye sıfat olduğu için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent form is plural, with singulars like meşec, meşic, or meşic; most exegetes gloss it as mixtures.
rows.anchor: “sebeb - esbâb”, “ketif - ektâf”, “şehîd - eşhâd” gibi cemi‘olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a singular it pictures one mixture of combined parts; as a plural it pictures multiple mixtures whose components are themselves mixtures.
rows.anchor: müfrede sıfat olması “zâti emşâcin” takdîrinde olarak emşâclı yahut ahlâttan ibaret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ahlāṭ” are mixed fluids such as blood, bile, phlegm, and lymph; the nuṭfa’s complete composition is known only to its Maker.
rows.anchor: kan, safra, sevdâ, balgam “lenfa” (lymphe) gibi karışık kimyevî mürekkebât-ı mahsûsaya “ahlât” ıtlak olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many understand the mixture as male and female fluids combining in the womb at fertilization, but Elmalılı considers this too late because the product is then called an embryo or clinging clot.
rows.anchor: ihtilâtı, yani telkīh hâli diye telakkī etmişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others explain the mixtures as blood and similar humors.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da kan ve emsâli ahlât demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to explain the nuṭfa’s “roots” or essential lines; Elmalılı reads these as formative traits embedded in the germ cell.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd Hazretleri’nden “nutfenin urûku”

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatada is reported to explain “amshāj” as colors and stages; Elmalılı applies this to the successive stages before conception and in embryonic development.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den “elvân ve etvâr”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is neither self-existent and perfect nor made as a simple creature in one instant; it develops through long stages as earlier, unrecognized materials are filtered, mixed, and cultivated.
rows.anchor: dehrin bidâyetinden beri devir devir, tavır tavır yaratılagelmiş gayr-i mezkur şeylerin süzülüp birbirlerine katıla katıla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complex nuṭfa and the vast development from it to a human cannot arise from autonomous nature; nature is dependent, while the Creator wills, composes, and cultivates.
rows.anchor: hüküm tabiatın değil, ona hâkim olan Hâlık ve Sâni‘Hak teâlâ’nındır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human to test him with responsibilities, duties, senses, and hardships, not to leave him purposeless; this links to 67:2 and 75:40.
rows.anchor: onu mübtelâ kılmak üzere evire çevire yani o insanı öyle yaratıp artık bitti diye südâ ve mühmel bırakıvermek için değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the human hearing and seeing so he can perceive revealed and created signs, understand through insight, and fulfill his responsibilities.
rows.anchor: tenzîlî, tekvînî âyât ve delâili işitecek, görecek, basîretle bilip ona göre şuur ile vazifesini yapacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After many stages, the human receives a distinct spiritual creation and remains a traveler through life, death, and a further life; this connects to 71:14 and 23:14.
rows.anchor: bambaşka[^16] bir rûhânî hilkate mazhar edilmiş, semî‘basîr mevt ve hayat geçitleriyle mübtelâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who does not truly hear, see, and consider duties to the Lord is unworthy of the title “human”; this definition is deeper than “rational animal.”
rows.anchor: hakkıyla semî‘basîr olmayan ve Rabbine karşı vazifelerini düşünmeyen kimseler “insan” unvânına lâyık değildirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testing clause gathers Qur’anic obligations, especially the human trials, hardship, reward, and punishment described in al-Mulk, al-Qiyama, and later surahs.
rows.anchor: نَّبْتَلِيهِ kaydı umumiyetle Kur’an’da beyan olunagelen mükellefiyetlerin hepsine işaret olmakla beraber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description “seeing” specially recalls the statement that the human is a witness against himself in 75:14.
rows.anchor: بَصِيرًا vasfının yine Sûre-i Kıyâme’de geçen

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Sıddîk
rows.claim: Al-Razi reports that Abu Bakr wished the human’s creation had ended before the testing stage, expressing his awareness of human incompleteness and the burden of future duties.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Sıddîk bu âyeti işittiği vakit يَا لَيْتـَهَا كَانَتْ تَمَّتْ فَلاَ نـُبْتـَلَى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses condense humanity’s delayed creation, successive refinement, spiritual nature, dependence on the Creator, and destiny under a law of testing and responsibility.
rows.anchor: bu iki âyet insanın hilkat tarihinde hikmet-i teahhuru, geçirdiği ıstıfâ mertebeleriyle sûret-i tekvîni hâli ve istikbâli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although death does not exhaust human destiny, the human travels toward the Lord and toward either the Fire or bliss, as stated in 75:30 and 75:12.
rows.anchor: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمَسَاقُ ve إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided path is true Islam, leading directly to God and His pure blessings; it is the path described in 75:30, 75:12, and 53:42 and in the Opening chapter.
rows.anchor: Kur’an ile davet olunan hak İslâm dinidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sets revealed and created, transmitted and rational signs in the world and within people, and gives them hearing, sight, and insight to show their origin, destination, and duties.
rows.anchor: tenzîlî ve tekvînî, naklî ve aklî âyetler, deliller, alâmetler nasb u ikāme ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude means recognizing guidance, believing with good intent, following the right path, enduring hardship, and moving toward perfection.
rows.anchor: Rabbine şükretmek üzere iman ve hüsn-i niyetle o Hak yoluna sülûk edip mihnetlere göğüs gererek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ingratitude means choosing disbelief, avoiding responsibility and moral growth, and acting as though one neither hears nor sees; guidance was shown in either case.
rows.anchor: teklif ve tekemmülden kaçınarak, bu irşad ve hidâyete karşı, işitmez, görmezceden gelerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast encourages gratitude and warns against disbelief, offering a concise promise and threat like 41:40.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan şükre tergīb, bir taraftan da küfürden tahzir için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has prepared chains, shackles, and a blazing Fire for unbelievers; people with insight should avoid disbelief rather than choose these punishments.
rows.anchor: çünkü Biz kâfirler için zincirler, tomruklar ve bir sa‘îr, çılgın bir ateş hazırlamışızdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ebrār” is the plural of “barr” (or “bārr”), the fully good and obedient person; it can also mean one who fulfills God’s rights and vows.
rows.anchor: “Ebrâr” “berr”in cem‘idir, “rabb - erbâb” gibi.

rows.speaker: Hasan
rows.claim: Hasan is reported to define the righteous as one who does not harm even an ant and is not content with evil.
rows.anchor: Hasan’dan “karıncayı incitmez, şerre râzı olmaz kimse” diye de mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points readers to 2:177 and 3:92 for the meaning of righteousness.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’da, لَّيْسَ ٱلْبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bārr” means one who performs goodness and benevolence, and also one who is faithful to a covenant or oath.
rows.anchor: iyilik ve ihsan yapan, bir de ahdinde ve yemîninde sâdık olan mânalarına gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the grateful “the righteous” defines them and explains their entitlement to high honors: gratitude is practical, fulfilled through goodness, charity, benevolence, and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: şükürden murad şükr-i amelî olup bunun birr ü hayr ve ihsan ve sadakāt ile îfâ olunacağına tenbihtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous will drink in the afterlife, just as the unbelievers’ burning in the Fire describes their afterlife fate.
rows.anchor: ebrârın da şürblerinden murad âhiretteki şürbleri demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bukra” covers early morning through noon and “aṣīl” afternoon through evening; together the command spans the day and includes morning, noon, and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: bunda sabah, öğleyin, ikindi namazları dâhil olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From the night” means some portion of the night; the command to prostrate explains remembrance as prayer, using a part (prostration) to mean the whole.
rows.anchor: burada “fâ” ile فَٱسْجُدْ emri, وَٱذْكُرِ emrini de beyan ederek ondan da murad namaz olduğunu anlatır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night portion denotes the evening and night prayers.
rows.anchor: Gecenin bazı cüz’ü de akşam ve yatsı demek olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Long night worship recalls the command to perform tahajjud and signals that the waiting for God’s decree may feel long; the Prophet and, indirectly, the community should stay awake in worship and preparation.
rows.anchor: Peygamber’e teheccüdün vücûbuna tenbih olmakla beraber Rabbinin hükmü gelinceye kadar sabır emrolunan müddetin uzun bir gece gibi geleceğine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers love the immediate world and abandon the heavy day ahead, which is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: Bu ağır gün önlerindeki kıyamettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Shaddadnā asrahum” literally describes tight binding; here it means the body’s joints and connective structures, including vessels, nerves, and muscles.
rows.anchor: hilkat bendleri, bedenlerin mafsallarını bağlayan urûk u a‘sâb ve adalât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the bodily binding idiomatically as “we bound their swaddling.”
rows.anchor: Biz bu “şedd-i esr”i mealde “kundaklarını bağlamak” tâbiriyle ifade etmeyi muvâfık bulduk.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Changing their likenesses” may mean destroying people and creating replacements, reading the word from “misl.”
rows.anchor: “kendilerini ihlâk eder, yerlerine diğer misillerini halkederiz” mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers changing their attributes or appearance, deriving the word from “masal”; 56:61 makes this sense clear.
rows.anchor: mânasına “mîm”in fethiyle “mesel”den olarak tebdîl-i sıfât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human will is real but not independent: responsibility belongs to the servant, while judgment and the governing will belong to God.
rows.anchor: onun mutlak olmayıp meşiyyet-i ilâhiyeye tevâfuk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot shape their destiny at whim; they remain responsible within God’s will, while God is unbound and sets the path, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: kul mukadderâtını keyfine göre çizemez, meşiyyet-i ilâhiye dairesinde mes’uldür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God shows two paths, admits whom He wills into mercy, and has prepared painful punishment for wrongdoers; humanity is tested between these outcomes.
rows.anchor: biri rahmetine, biri azâbına giden iki yol göstermiştir. İşte insan gösterilen bu iki yolun arasında mübtelâ olmak üzere yaratılmıştır.
